## Monthly Budget Fit Check

For a **$4,200** net income, your fixed costs total **$2,495**. That leaves **$1,705** before discretionary spending and savings.

## 50/30/20 vs Zero-Based Budgeting

| Method | How it handles your money | Savings target | Dining out | Entertainment control | Fit for your situation |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 50/30/20 | 50% needs, 30% wants, 20% savings/debt | **$840** | Usually flexible inside wants | Moderate | Simple, but easier to overspend on wants |
| Zero-based budgeting | Every dollar is assigned a job | **You set it directly** | Set a hard cap | Strong | Better control and better match for your goals |

### Your numbers under each method

- **Needs total:** $2,495
- **50/30/20 needs cap:** $2,100 → your current fixed costs are **$395 over** the needs target
- **50/30/20 wants cap:** $1,260 → must cover dining out, entertainment, and all other flexible spending
- **50/30/20 savings target:** $840 → meets your “at least $700” goal

## Budget Recommendation for Your Spending Pattern

### Best fit: **Zero-based budgeting**
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/currency-rupee.svg

- It gives you a **hard limit** for dining out and entertainment.
- It works better if you tend to **overspend on entertainment**, because every category gets a preset amount.
- It lets you protect savings first, then assign the rest intentionally.

### Why 50/30/20 is weaker here
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/sliders.svg

- Your fixed costs already take a large share of income.
- The standard 50/30/20 split is **less precise** for your actual bills.
- Entertainment and dining out can easily drift if they stay inside one broad “wants” bucket.

## Practical Zero-Based Plan

| Category | Monthly Amount |
|---|---:|
| Rent | $1,450 |
| Utilities | $180 |
| Transit | $95 |
| Groceries | $420 |
| Student loan | $260 |
| Phone | $55 |
| Subscriptions | $35 |
| Dining out | **$250 max** |
| Entertainment | **$150–$250 cap** |
| Savings | **$700 minimum** |
| Other buffer | **$305–$405** |

### What this means
- If you save **$700**, and cap dining out at **$250**, you still have room for entertainment and a small buffer.
- A good zero-based setup would likely assign:
  - **Savings:** $700–$840
  - **Dining out:** $250 max
  - **Entertainment:** a separate hard cap, not shared with dining
  - **Buffer:** keep the rest for irregular costs or extra savings
